stances.claim: Invoking China's April 13, 2009 Note Verbale and the November 2018 Memorandum of Agreement is not a waiver of the arbitral award; these are complementary diplomatic instruments because the arbitral body has no enforcement power and the Philippines lacks the military, political, or economic clout to compel obedience.

Duterte's raising of the award at the UN was necessary precisely 'to avoid an implied waiver of the rights granted therein' -- recognition of which path is necessary to preserve the award even while pursuing parallel diplomatic channels.

The friendly stance has produced concrete benefits: Filipinos allowed to fish in Scarborough Shoal; no Chinese airports or missile silos there; no assertion of a 12-nautical-mile territorial sea overlapping the PH EEZ; and recognition of broader economic, political, and trade relationships.

US defense pacts (MDT, EDCA) do not obligate the United States to protect the Philippine EEZ; the US 'will act only when its national interest is threatened,' as shown by the US conducting freedom-of-navigation operations in the SCS while not confronting China's fortifications of seven Spratly features -- two of which (Mabini Reef and Panganiban Reef) lie in the PH EEZ.

Peaceful negotiation and mediation are preferable to litigation or arbitration even in international disputes because 'litigants are never completely satisfied with imposed judgments or awards,' and litigation 'may decide legal issues' but 'do[es] not heal broken relationships' which can produce generational enmities; mediated solutions restore prior amiable relationships.

notable_anecdotes: Citation of Capt. James E. Fanell (US Pacific Fleet intelligence chief for Pacific operations) on Chinese fortifications and militarization of seven Spratly features -- using American intelligence sourcing to undermine reliance on American defense pacts.

Identification of two Spratly features in the PH EEZ now Chinese-fortified -- Mabini Reef and Panganiban Reef -- with the column's author bearing the name of one of the reefs, a quiet personal-stake disclosure.
CJ's frank concession that 'I never suggested that' the award be waived -- modeling the practice of correcting reader mischaracterizations in print rather than letting them stand.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban answers seven follow-up questions from readers of his prior six Sunday columns on the South China Sea dispute. He clarifies that invoking China's April 13, 2009 Note Verbale to the UN Secretary General (an implied admission of Philippine maritime entitlements) and the November 2018 Memorandum of Agreement (60-40 sharing in PH favor) does not waive the July 12, 2016 arbitral award -- these are complementary diplomatic channels necessary because the arbitral body lacks enforcement power and the Philippines lacks the military, political, and economic clout to compel China's obedience. Duterte's raising of the award at the UN, he explains, was necessary precisely 'to avoid an implied waiver.' The friendly stance has produced concrete benefits -- Filipinos allowed to fish at Scarborough Shoal, no Chinese airports or missile silos there, no 12-nautical-mile territorial-sea assertion overlapping the EEZ, and recognized economic-political-trade relationships. US defense pacts (MDT and EDCA) do not obligate the US to protect the Philippine EEZ; CJ cites Capt. James E. Fanell of the US Pacific Fleet on Chinese fortifications of seven Spratly features (two -- Mabini Reef and Panganiban Reef -- within the PH EEZ) to show that even the US conducts freedom-of-navigation operations without confronting them. The column closes with CJ's jurist-as-mediator philosophy: peaceful negotiation or mediation toward win-win solutions is preferable to imposed judgments or awards because 'litigants are never completely satisfied' and litigation 'may decide legal issues, but they do not heal broken relationships' which can produce 'bruised egos,' 'vicious hostilities,' and 'generational enmities.'
